text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- CHILEANS PAY 30 PCT OVER BASE PRICE FOR CERJ

Rio de Janeiro state's first privatization was a success as a consortium led by Chile's Chilectra paid 605.3 million reais for Cerj power firm, some 30.27 percent higher than the state-set minimum price.
-- ARGENTINE'S INTERESTED IN SOUTH BRANCH RAILROAD
Among the groups interested in bidding on the South Branch of Brazil's federal railway system is a consortium led by Argentina's Industria Metalurgica Pescarmona group.
-- ALCOA TO INVEST 450 MILLION REAIS IN BRAZIL PROJECT
Alcoa Aluminio S.A. will invest some 450 million reais in the Tucurui hydropower project and plans to focus Brazilian investments in coming years on privatizations and the country's energy sector.
O GLOBO
-- CARDOSO REFUSES TO BARGAIN FOR RE-ELECTION BILL APPROVAL

President Fernando Henrique Cardoso said Wednesday he refuses to bargain for approval of his proposed re-election bill by backsliding on plans to privatize state mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce.
-- REDUNDANCY PLAN AFFECTS NON-STAFF DOCTORS AND TEACHERS
The Brazilian government's Voluntary Redundancy Program to reduce the federal workforce begins today and will include even non-staff doctors, teachers and other workers.
-- RIO 2004 OLYMPICS BID FACES ITS GREATEST TEST SO FAR
Rio de Janeiro's deam of becoming the site of the 2004 Olympic Games faces its greatest test today with the arrival of an International Olympic Committee mission that will evaluate the city.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- ACROSS BRAZIL, A SCARCITY OF TRIPLE VACCINE
The Health Ministry said Brazil is facing a scarcity of triple vaccine for whooping cough, diphteria and tetanus for babies across 25 states and the federal district.
-- FEDERAL GOVERNMENT WOULD GET BANESPA SHARES

Sao Paulo's government would pass on to the Brazilian federal government shares of state bank Banespa under a proposed renegotiation of the state's debt to Brasilia. The proposal was unveiled by the Finance Ministry.
-- INFANT MORTALITY RATE IN NORTHEAST CITY RISES 384 PCT
The mortality rate of babies born in November at the largest maternity facility in the northeastern Brazilian city of Fortaleza has jumped 96 percent from last year and 384 percent since 1994.
Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- James Craig, Sao Paulo newsroom 5511 232 4411
